claude.rationale: gap_45=0: PE REIT II's customer-facing product (the grocery-anchored shopping-center portfolio, 321 centers) crossed into PECO, but the operational processes that ran those centers were ALREADY PECO's — PECO's affiliate (PE-NTR II) had managed PE REIT II's day-to-day operations since inception, so product and its producing processes were coherently under PECO's existing internally-managed organization at closing rather than mismatched. gap_56=0: PE REIT II "had no employees" and its executive officers were already PECO/affiliate officers; the terminated advisory/property-management agreements were with PECO's own affiliate, so no processes crossed the boundary detached from their operating people — the operating organization was PECO's continuing internal team throughout. The advisory-agreement termination removed external fees but bridged nothing external because operations were already internal to the acquirer, so no product-vs-process or process-vs-people structural mismatch is documented at closing.

gemini.rationale: PECO already managed PE REIT II prior to the merger, meaning the operational processes (T5) and the organization (T6) were already aligned and provided by PECO. At closing, PE REIT II's assets (T4) transferred to PECO, and the external advisory agreements were terminated because PECO internalized the management. There was no structural mismatch between product and process (gap_45 = 0) or process and organization (gap_56 = 0) because PECO already ran the operations and continued to do so.
